statement: The operation-ledger quorum-spread hold cannot defer its own documented cure: once the spread sequence reaches a surplus placement with every distinct node occupied, the fenced standalone-safe surplus REMOVE that drains the hot node is admissible (or the hold disengages on distinct-nodes-at-target), so the hold always has a reachable release path.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Whichever route is chosen (cure-class exemption for the fenced surplus REMOVE, or hold disengagement when distinct voter nodes reach target), the priority surplus-REMOVE placement fence, count/diversity monotonic safety, and the self-move serialization hold remain fully engaged; only the quorum-spread hold classification may change.

Two candidate routes, deliberately not pre-decided: (A) add a cure move class to OPERATION_LEDGER_HOLD_ENGAGEMENT_BY_MOVE_CLASS for a REMOVE whose source is the concentrated partition's surplus replica and which passes the surplus fence; (B) make evaluateLedgerPartitionConcentration disengage (or mark spread-unactionable) when distinctVoterNodeIds.length >= targetReplicaCount so the ordinary drain path runs. Route B touches the evaluator consumed by admission and release paths; route A touches the hold policy matrix in the operation-ledger-self-move-waiter-fairness quest family's territory. The decision needs the fence quest history (priority-surplus-remove-authoritative-placement-fence, exhausted) and hold-policy review question in operation-ledger-hold-policy.js:24.

Deterministic-ish repro: user-table-metadata-fanout residual (~1-in-3 post Face A+C): cluster reaches 4 voters at 2-1-1 (seed 2, joiners 1+1), concentration reports overTarget true / spreadActionable true / feasibleTargetNodeIds [], and across 22+ pump-driven planning cycles NO surplus REMOVE is ever minted - zero removal activity in the entire run (fanout-loop-1 captured log: only provisioning-deferral and raft-truncation-refusal messages). The hold policy's own comment (operation-ledger-hold-policy.js:107-113) documents REMOVE as the drain step while classifying it DEPENDENT, which the engaged quorum-spread hold defers: the hold defers its own cure.

The interaction contract ALREADY EXISTS and this bug argues against it: docs/specs/decision-tables/operation-ledger-hold-engagement.json (owner operation-ledger-hold-policy.js, boundary rebalancer_admission) carries invariant cure-stays-admissible - 'The move class that cures a hold is never deferred by that hold (CL-013)'. Today's LEDGER_QUORUM_SPREAD_CURE_MOVE_TYPES excludes the drain REMOVE the policy's own comment calls the cure sequence's final step, so at 2-1-1 the hold has no release path: either the implementation under-classifies the cure (violating the invariant) or the DT's cure definition is too narrow (the invariant needs the drain row). Closure extends THAT decision table, and per models/CL-INDEX.md (DT7 doctrine: design-class liveness bugs are proven by TLC counterexample/fixed pairs) adds or extends a model in the incremental-replace-spread / ledger-selfmove-remint family with a liveness property that fails on today's matrix and passes on the chosen route. Sibling artifacts to keep coherent: placement-cure-admission-lane.json, replica-placement-cure-condition.json, and the CL-013 closure record.
